description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Includes:
- Supports use of IETF BCP 47 language tags as defined by RFC 5646, checking that a tag is well-formed, or valid against a copy of the IANA Language Subtag Registry.
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- Bcp47LanguageTag.ExtendedLanguageSubtags, VariantSubtags and ExtensionSubtags, and Bcp47KeyedSubtag.Subtags, now return IReadOnlyList<T> instead of an array; use Count instead of Length, and copy the list (for example with ToArray()) if you need an array you can change.
- The matchTimeout overloads of Bcp47LanguageTag.Create and TryCreate, Bcp47LanguageTagBuilder.WithTimeout, and the IBcp47LanguageTagBuilderStepWithTimeout and IBcp47LanguageTagBuilderStepWithTimeoutNext interfaces are removed. Drop the timeout argument or the WithTimeout step; behaviour is unchanged.
- Subtag Registry records are immutable. ISubtagRegistryRecord is no longer an IList<Tuple<string, object>>; read raw fields from its Fields property. SubtagRegistryTagRecordBase.Type is a SubtagRegistryRecordType, and Description, Prefix and Comments are IReadOnlyList<string>. SubtagRegistryFieldAttribute and the protected GetPropertyValue/GetPropertyValues helpers are removed, and the record classes are sealed with internal constructors. A malformed date reads as absent instead of throwing FormatException.
- Bcp47LanguageTag.PrimaryLanguageSubtag is now a string? and returns null instead of the empty string on a private use or grandfathered language tag; test for null instead of an empty string.
- The builder's UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49AreaByAlpha2CountryCode) and UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49AreaByAlpha3CountryCode) overloads are removed; use UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area) for an area made up of more than one country, or UsingRegionSubtag(Iso3166Part1Alpha2Country) for a country.
- `Bcp47LanguageTag.IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` is removed; use `IsWellFormed` for the grammar or `IsValid` with a `SubtagRegistry` for validity.
- `Bcp47LanguageTag.Check*Subtag` and the string steps of `Bcp47LanguageTagBuilder` check only the shape of a subtag and look nothing up, so `CheckRegionSubtag("830")` is `true` and the builder accepts a subtag that is in your registry but not in an ISO list.
- `SubtagRegistry` moves to the `DataStandardizer.LanguageTag` namespace, so it no longer needs an alias or the doubled name `SubtagRegistry.SubtagRegistry`; the types of its records move to `DataStandardizer.LanguageTag.Registry`.
- The packages no longer have a `net8.0` build. An application on .NET 8 or .NET 9 gets a .NET Standard build, without the APIs that only the `net10.0` build has, such as `DateOnly` and `TimeOnly` support. To keep those APIs, move the application to .NET 10.
- The `netstandard1.x` and `netstandard2.0` builds no longer list `JetBrains.Annotations` as a NuGet dependency. If your code uses its attributes and you got the package through DataStandardizer, add a reference to `JetBrains.Annotations` to your project.
- `SubtagRegistry.CreateFromContent`, `CreateFromFile` and `CreateFromStream`, and their async forms, now require the CRLF that RFC 5646 §3.1.1 ends every line with. The registry file that IANA publishes ends each line with a line feed alone, so load it with the new overloads that take `SubtagRegistryLoadOptions.AcceptBareLineFeed`.

New:
- Bcp47LanguageTag's ReadOnlySpan<char> overloads and AsSpan() are now available on netstandard1.1.
- SubtagRegistry.TryGetSubtag, IsGrandfathered and FileDate, and a list of the records of each type, such as Languages, Scripts and GrandfatheredTags.
- `LanguageTagConformance`, `Bcp47LanguageTag.Conformance` and `Create`/`TryCreate` overloads that take a conformance, with `IsoCodeLists` as an explicit opt-in to the ISO code lists.
- `Bcp47LanguageTag.IsValid` overloads that take a `LanguageTagConformance`, for checking a tag against the ISO code lists without creating it.
- `Bcp47LanguageTagBuilder.WithConformance`, an optional first step that chooses what `Build` checks.
- `SubtagRegistryLoadOptions`, taken by new `SubtagRegistry.CreateFromContent`, `CreateFromFile` and `CreateFromStream` overloads and their async forms, accepts a line feed alone at the end of a line (`AcceptBareLineFeed`) or a last line with no line break (`AcceptMissingFinalLineBreak`).

Fixed:
- Comments on a registry record returns every Comments field, not only the first.
- `LanguageTagConformance.IsoCodeLists` rejects three-letter ISO 639 codes of languages that have an ISO 639-1 code, such as `eng`, `deu` and `fra`, as RFC 5646 §2.2.1 requires.
- `LanguageTagConformance.IsoCodeLists` accepts the ISO 639-3 code `hbs`; it is still not valid against the IANA subtag registry.
- `Bcp47LanguageTag.IsValid` and `Create` with a `SubtagRegistry` no longer accept a tag that isn't well-formed, or that uses a subtag where the registry's record for it doesn't have the shape RFC 5646 §2.1 requires, such as `enochian-yue` against a registry that has a `language` record for `enochian`. This affects only registries with such records, not the IANA registry.
- The `netstandard1.1` build depends on `System.Net.Http` 4.3.4 instead of 4.3.2, which has a known vulnerability.
- Debuggers can step into the packages' source through Source Link.
- `SubtagRegistry.CreateFromContent`, `CreateFromFile` and `CreateFromStream`, and their async forms, throw `FormatException`, naming the line, for a registry that isn't in the record-jar format of RFC 5646 §3.1.1, instead of folding a line that isn't indented into the field before it, reading a tab as a space, skipping blank lines, or dropping a record that has no `File-Date`, `Subtag` or `Tag` field.
- Loading a `SubtagRegistry` throws `FormatException` for a tag or subtag record with no `Type`, a `Type` that RFC 5646 §3.1.3 doesn't define, or one that doesn't go with its `Subtag` or `Tag` field, instead of loading it as `SubtagRegistryRecordType.Unknown`.
- Loading a `SubtagRegistry` throws `FormatException` for a `File-Date`, `Added` or `Deprecated` field that isn't an RFC 3339 full-date, instead of reading `FileDate` and `Added` as 0001-01-01 and `Deprecated` as `null`.
- Loading a `SubtagRegistry` throws `FormatException` for a registry whose first record isn't the `File-Date` record, that has a second `File-Date` record or another field in it, that has a tag or subtag record with no `Description` or `Added` field, or a record where a field other than `Description`, `Comments` and `Prefix` appears twice (RFC 5646 §3.1.2). Before, `SubtagRegistry.FileDate` could be `null`, `Added` could read as 0001-01-01, and a repeated field was ignored.

Changed:
- Reading ExtendedLanguageSubtags, VariantSubtags or ExtensionSubtags no longer copies the subtags on each read.
- Registry record properties are parsed once when the registry is loaded, so reading them no longer converts the field on each read.
- The netstandard1.1 build no longer depends on System.ComponentModel.TypeConverter.
- Creating a `Bcp47LanguageTag` without a subtag registry now checks only that it matches the ABNF of RFC 5646 §2.1, so tags such as `zz` and `de-1901-1901` are accepted; creating one with a registry still checks validity (RFC 5646 §2.2.9).
- The message of `LanguageTagFormatException` names the conformance class that failed.
- The netstandard1.x and netstandard2.0 builds now carry nullable annotations, so projects on C# 8 or later with nullable enabled get null warnings from them.
- `SubtagRegistry.ToString()` and the records' `ToString()` write CRLF at the end of every line, the last one included, as RFC 5646 §3.1.1 requires, instead of `Environment.NewLine` with no line break after the last line, so the default `CreateFrom…` methods load what they write.
